payload.title: Moving magnet: illustrative Faraday-law experiment

model.title: Moving magnet: illustrative Faraday-law experiment
model.description: Unqualified proposal for human review: bounded axial motion, normalized magnetic flux, signed EMF and resistive current for an apparatus-first teaching experiment.
assumptions: All defaults are adjustable illustrative examples, not specifications of a real magnet or coil.

The coil normal and positive axial direction are +x. Positive pole orientation gives positive flux along that normal. Positive EMF follows the right-hand circulation about +x; the labelled positive meter terminal follows this convention.

Flux per turn is Φ=p(V_scale T_scale)exp[-(x/L)^2]. L=0.1 m, V_scale=0.001 V and T_scale=1 s give a flux scale of 0.001 V s. Flux outputs are explicitly normalized because the scalar unit vocabulary does not include magnetic flux.
For fixed pole orientation and turns, EMF=-N(dΦ/dx)v=2NpV_scale(T_scale v/L)(x/L)exp[-(x/L)^2]. This is differentiation of the stated illustrative flux, not a calibrated magnetic-field prediction.
Motion is a constant-velocity trial: x=x_start+v t. Moving the start-position control repositions the magnet between trials; it must not animate displacement with an unrelated velocity.

Time playback uses time, step 0.02 s and playback speed 1. Changing start_position, velocity, polarity, turns or circuit restarts time atomically at zero. Trial initial position is start_position and initial velocity is velocity.
Polarity is restricted to -1 or +1; turns to integers; circuit to 0 or 1. Pole reversal and changes in turns are between-trial reconfiguration, not simulated induction pulses.
Resistance is fixed at 10 ohm even when turns change. The closed circuit is purely resistive and quasi-static; open-circuit current is zero while coil EMF may remain nonzero.

Positive current produces a field along +x. For positive flux, approach on the negative-x side gives negative current opposing increasing flux; withdrawal gives positive current opposing its decrease. Reversing the pole reverses these signs.
Apparatus readouts and current-direction indications must use the same EMF, current and engagement outputs. A voltage indication across the coil is distinct from an ammeter indication in the loop.
Supported bounds: position ±0.6 m, velocity ±0.1 m/s, normalized per-turn flux ±1, normalized linkage ±500, EMF ±6 V and current ±0.6 A. These conservative bounds hold over every allowed combination.
limitations: Illustrative axial geometry and identical flux linkage for all turns; no calibrated predictions for an actual magnet or apparatus.
No self-inductance, switching transients, detailed charge dynamics or simulated mechanical back-reaction. Lenz-law opposition is explained from current direction, not a calculated force.
Constant-speed passes and stationary trials only; arbitrary accelerated dragging is not represented.
No induction pulses from pole reversal, turn-count changes or between-trial repositioning are modeled.
This mathematical stage supplies no geometry or inspectable spatial parts. Apparatus-first presentation, labels, inspection and guided prompts require a subsequent rendering stage.
The schema has no dedicated input-default, range or time_experiment fields; their required values and playback contract are explicitly declared here and in input descriptions.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How does moving a bar magnet through a coil generate electricity? Build an interactive CBSE Class 12 electromagnetic-induction experiment with a visible magnet, coil, wire and signed meter. Let me move the magnet, reverse its pole, change coil turns and open or close the circuit. Show motion and the resulting EMF and current on the apparatus, with inspectable parts and guided comparisons. Use a stated illustrative magnetic-flux model consistent with Faraday and Lenz laws; distinguish EMF from current and show zero EMF when the magnet is stationary. Make the experiment the main view, with any graph as a supporting view.

limits: Illustrative axial model, not calibrated magnet predictions; all turns share identical flux linkage.
Flux per turn is p(0.001 V s)exp[-(x/0.1 m)^2]; EMF=-N(dΦ/dx)v. Positive coil normal and motion are +x; positive meter polarity follows right-hand circulation about +x.
Positive current produces a field along +x, opposing the change in flux; no force or mechanical back-reaction is calculated.
Fixed total resistance is 10 ohm regardless of turns. Closed-loop current is EMF/R; open-loop current is zero, not necessarily EMF.
No self-inductance, switching transients, detailed charge dynamics or induction pulses from reconfiguration.
Constant-speed or stationary trials only: x=start_position+velocity*time. No arbitrary accelerated dragging.
Start position spans -0.2 to 0.2 m; velocity spans -0.1 to 0.1 m/s; time spans 0 to 4 s. Full travel spans -0.6 to 0.6 m.

Defaults: start position -0.2 m, velocity +0.1 m/s, time 0 s, polarity +1, 100 turns and closed circuit. Polarity choices are -1 and +1; integer turns span 1 to 500; circuit choices are open and closed only. These are illustrative settings, not apparatus specifications. parts.label: Coil · +x normal
parts.explanation: This wound wire links magnetic flux, a measure of magnetic field passing through its loops. Changing that flux produces an EMF, or driving voltage.

parts.label: Bar magnet · labelled N and S poles
parts.explanation: The magnet moves through the coil along x. Reversing its poles reverses the signed flux.

parts.label: Connecting wire and switch contacts
parts.explanation: This wire connects the coil, meter and switch into a loop. Current can flow around the loop only when the switch closes the gap.

parts.label: Signed meter · EMF (V) / current (A)
parts.explanation: The voltage display shows EMF across the coil; the ammeter display shows current around the loop. Plus and minus signs show direction using the marked terminal convention.

parts.label: Open / closed switch
parts.explanation: This blade closes or breaks the conducting path. An open path stops loop current even when the coil has EMF.

experiments.title: Rest, approach and withdrawal
experiments.prompt: Set starting position to -0.1 m and keep the circuit closed. Predict EMF at rest, then compare velocities +0.05, +0.1 and -0.1 m/s at time zero.
experiments.explanation: At the same position, reversing velocity reverses EMF and doubling speed doubles its magnitude. Zero velocity gives zero EMF despite nonzero flux. The smooth Gaussian flux profile is illustrative, not calibrated. Positive current produces a +x field opposing the flux change; force is not simulated.

experiments.title: Reverse the poles
experiments.prompt: Use starting position -0.1 m, velocity +0.1 m/s and a closed circuit. Predict the EMF sign when polarity changes from +1 to -1; compare at time zero.
experiments.explanation: Pole reversal reverses signed flux and EMF for otherwise identical trials. This is between-trial reconfiguration, not a modeled induction pulse. Numerical readouts show calculated values; the static meter mesh does not display numbers.

experiments.title: Increase coil turns
experiments.prompt: At starting position -0.1 m and velocity +0.1 m/s, compare 100 and 200 turns at time zero. Predict EMF and closed-loop current.
experiments.explanation: EMF scales directly with turns under the identical-flux-linkage assumption. Closed-loop current also scales because resistance remains fixed at 10 ohm. Turn changes restart the trial without modeled reconfiguration pulses.

experiments.title: Open the circuit
experiments.prompt: Use starting position -0.1 m and velocity +0.1 m/s. Predict current and EMF when the circuit opens; compare both numerical readouts at time zero.
experiments.explanation: Opening the circuit sets loop current to zero without requiring zero coil EMF. When closed, current equals EMF divided by the fixed 10-ohm resistance. Switching transients and self-inductance are excluded.

controls.help: Sets the initial axial position relative to the coil center and restarts the trial.
Sets constant signed velocity; zero holds the magnet still, and changes restart the trial.
Advances the four-second constant-velocity trial and updates position, flux, EMF and current.
Reverses signed flux and EMF between trials; changing orientation restarts time without modeling a reversal pulse.
Sets integer coil turns and restarts the trial; EMF scales with turns while resistance stays fixed at 10 ohm.
Opening stops loop current, not necessarily EMF; changing the switch restarts time without switching transients.

time_experiment.explanation: The fixed four-second trial starts at x=start_position with velocity=velocity and follows x=start_position+velocity*time. EMF is the analytic Faraday-law derivative of the illustrative Gaussian flux; current is resistive with fixed 10-ohm resistance. Every non-time setting change atomically resets time to zero. No transient response or electrical time constant is modeled.

coverage.explanation: The illustrative differentiable flux profile supplies the Faraday-law EMF. Current direction explains Lenz-law opposition without simulating force.
Controls support constant-speed motion, rest, discrete pole orientation, integer turns and circuit continuity; reconfiguration restarts each trial.
Separate numerical readouts distinguish signed EMF from current. Rest gives zero motion-induced EMF; opening the circuit gives zero current without requiring zero EMF.
Inspect the apparatus parts and terminal convention. Inspection alone does not establish simulated causality, and the static meter mesh does not display numerical values.
Four guided comparisons cover rest, direction, speed, polarity, turns and continuity at matched positions. Numerical observations support the apparatus-first experience without requiring a graph.

outcomes: Explain how changing magnetic flux linkage produces EMF, using an explicitly illustrative model consistent with Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws.
Manipulate magnet position and motion, reverse its pole, vary coil turns, and open or close the circuit.
Observe signed EMF and current on the apparatus; distinguish induced EMF from current and verify zero motion-induced EMF when the magnet is stationary.
Inspect the magnet, coil, connecting wire and signed meter, with visible motion and electrical indications.
Use guided comparisons to relate motion direction, speed, polarity, coil turns and circuit continuity to the observations, keeping graphs secondary.

repair_actions.rule: Retries require the existing explicit retry flow. Never edit accepted artifact hashes or automatically spend provider requests.

scene_revision.feedback: Keep the accepted equations, layout and 3D geometry unchanged. Improve the learning controls: polarity must be kind choices with only -1 and +1 named orientations; circuit must be kind choices with Open=0 and Closed=1. Do not expose fractional switches. Keep range controls for start_position, velocity and turns, with sensible presets. Retain time playback and atomic reset on all non-time setting changes; end_time_id=null because this is a fixed four-second trial, not a computed physical termination event. Preserve meaningful guided comparisons for stationary motion, reversing velocity, reversing polarity, number of turns and open circuit. Explain that the smooth flux profile is illustrative; current uses a fixed 10-ohm circuit and opening the circuit stops current without requiring zero EMF. Do not claim the static meter mesh displays numbers; numerical readouts show the calculated values.
